In hepatocellular carcinoma tissues and cell lines, MIF and cyclin D1 expression levels were significantly upregulated compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression, and both MIF and cyclin D1 expression positively correlated with tumor size. MIF knockdown inhibited the proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells and promoted apoptosis, but small interfering RNA against MIF did not influence the cell cycle in these cells. In an in vivo xenograft model, MIF knockdown reduced the tumor growth rate. In MIF-knockdown cells, Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax were upregulated, while cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK were downregulated. These findings indicate that MIF siRNA reduces proliferation and increases apoptosis in HCC cells.

In this review, we summarize the state of the art in the field of NASH and NASH-HCC with focus on immunobiology.
